title: runtime-deployment-sanity-and-benchmark-suite-acceptance-2026
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:

This document defines the deployment sanity acceptance criteria and the canonical benchmark suite used by the runtime team to gate runtime changes (kernels, scheduler, orchestration). It is intended for engineers running release validation, SREs owning rollout decisions, and release managers approving canaries.

Goal:

- Provide a compact, reproducible benchmark suite that exercises the common hot-paths across models, sequence lengths, batching shapes, and third-party accelerators.
- Define clear pass/fail acceptance criteria and automated checks that can be executed in CI or on pre-deploy staging clusters.
- Ensure performance regressions (latency, throughput, and cost-per-token) are caught before platform rollouts beyond canary.

Scope:

Applies to: kernel patches, scheduler policy changes, orchestration control plane releases that affect request routing/eviction, and quantization/runtime memory layout changes. Does not replace long-form lab benchmarks (see references).

Owner and Escalation:

- Suite owner: Runtime Performance Team (primary contact: Aisha Patel)
- On-call escalation: runtime-sre@redwood.ai -> Pager duty escalation per SRE rota

Acceptance Criteria (high level):

1) Functional: all sample generation and embedding endpoints return valid responses for the test corpus (no 5xx/errors)
2) Latency: p95 generation latency must not regress more than 10% vs baseline for the same commit, absolute p95 thresholds below: see table.
3) Throughput: end-to-end throughput for batched inference must remain within -15% of baseline on identical hardware profiles.
4) Cost: measured per-token GPU cycles (proxy: aggregate GPU utilization normalized by tokens/s) must not increase >8%.
5) Memory: peak GPU memory used must not exceed baseline + 50 MB for small models, +200 MB for large models.

Sanity matrix (text table):

| Test name | Model class | Sequence lengths | Concurrency / Batch shapes | Primary metric | Threshold |
|-----------|-------------|------------------|----------------------------|----------------|----------|
| gen-short-seq | small (7B) | 32 / 128 | 1, 8 | p95 latency | < 120ms (p95) |
| gen-long-seq | medium (13B) | 512 / 1024 | 1, 4 | p95 latency | < 650ms (p95) |
| batch-encoder | embedding (2B) | 128 | 32/64 | qps | >= baseline*0.85 |
| kv-cache-warm | session-heavy (7B) | 256 | 1 steady | tail latency | <= baseline + 10% |
| quantized-fidelity-check | quantized 4-bit (13B) | 128 | 4 | output match | top-5 token agreement >= 98% |

Note: baseline values are taken from the last green release tag (recorded in the benchmark registry). Absolute thresholds are pragmatic safety nets; primary gating is percentage regression relative to baseline.

Benchmark suite components and runner:

- bench-runner v2: our canonical harness (Go binary) used by CI. Configs live in repo: infra/benchmarks/bench-runner/configs/
- trace-collector: sidecar process that collects kernel timings, GPU utilization, and NVLink stats.
- shadow-replayer: replays production request surface for fidelity checks (sampled traces).
- model-profiles: YAML files describing model input shapes, cache-hit scenarios, and expected KV-cache behavior.

Example bench-runner config (YAML snippet):

-- bench_config:
   name: gen-short-seq-7b
   model: redwood/small-7b:2026-01
   seeds: 100
   sequence_lengths: [32, 128]
   concurrency: [1, 8]
   gpu_profile: p4d.24xlarge
   metrics: [p50, p95, p99, gpu_util, tokens_per_second]
   run_duration: 180

CI integration and automated checks:

- Pull request pipeline will run a lightweight subset (smoke) of the suite on a single accelerator host (duration ~15m).
- Merged commits to the release branch trigger a nightly full sanity run against the current baseline.
- Release candidate builds must pass the full suite in staging (see "Release gating" below) before canary rollout.

How to run locally (developer guide):

1) Checkout infra/benchmarks and build bench-runner: make bench-runner
2) Start a staging node with the same accelerator profile used in CI (use dev-k8s cluster): ./scripts/provision-staging --profile p4d
3) Upload the model bundle to the staging model registry: scripts/push-model --model redwood/small-7b:local
4) Run bench-runner with a config: ./bin/bench-runner --config configs/gen-short-seq-7b.yaml --collect-traces
5) Upload results to the benchmark registry: ./scripts/upload-results --run-id=local-$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)

Measurements and signal definitions:

- p95 latency: end-to-end wallclock time from request accept to final token (includes network hop to sidecar).
- token-rate: measured as tokens / GPU-second, aggregated over the run (proxy for cost per token).
- kernel-latency profile: distribution of kernel launch times collected by trace-collector (used for attributions).

Pass/fail automation rules (applied by bench-compare tool):

1) If any functional test returns non-2xx: FAIL
2) If p95 regression >10% on any generation test: WARNING (auto-fail unless triage-approved)
3) If throughput regression >15% or token-cost increase >8%: FAIL
4) If peak GPU memory exceeds the memory budget (per model): FAIL
5) Small regressions (p95 5-10%) open a performance ticket with attached traces; release can proceed only with a documented mitigations plan approved by the runtime performance lead.

Release gating and canary choreography:

- Staging green -> Canary 1 (1% traffic, 4 hours) -> Canary 2 (10% traffic, 8 hours) -> Gradual ramp to 100% (24–48 hours)
- Canary approval requires: pass of full sanity suite in staging, no SLO breaches in Canary 1, and no kernel exceptions in trace logs.
- If any SLO breach occurs during canary, rollback immediately to previous stable tag and open incident with the severity determined by the breach impact table below.

Severity and rollback table (text):

- Sev-1: total p95 regression >50% or >=1 service-wide 5xx per 1000 requests for 15m -> immediate rollback, stop rollout, incident declared.
- Sev-2: p95 regression >25% or sustained token-cost increase >20% for 30m -> pause rollout, mitigation plan within 4 hours.
- Sev-3: isolated regression for a single model class or marginal p95 regression 10–25% -> require patch and re-run of suite before reattempting rollout.

Runbook: triage steps on failing benchmark run:

1) Gather artifacts: bench-runner logs, trace-collector bundle, GPU-health metrics, bench-compare report.
2) Run bench-compare to produce diff vs baseline: ./bin/bench-compare --baseline last-green --run current-run-id
3) If failure maps to kernel hotspots, tag kernel-team and include kernel traces.
4) If failure maps to scheduler/policy (e.g., increased tail latencies under mixed shapes), repro in local lab with shadow-replayer and run scheduler-debug script.
5) For memory regressions, capture heap/profile: /scripts/capture-gpu-mem-snapshot.sh <node> and file a memory regression bug.

Known limitations and caveats:

- This suite intentionally focuses on representative shapes; it can miss rare production edge-cases. Use production shadow traces to complement the suite.
- External cloud neighbor noise (noisy GPUs) can affect throughput numbers; we mitigate by running three repeats and using median.
- Third-party accelerator quirks (driver versions and NVLink topology) must be documented per-hardware in infra/benchmarks/hardware-profiles/

Operational housekeeping:

- Bench results retention: raw traces stored for 90 days, aggregated metrics indefinitely in the benchmark registry.
- Baseline rotation: After a major release, the baseline is re-recorded. Baselines must be signed off by runtime performance lead.

References and links:

- infra/benchmarks/README (bench-runner usage)
- runtime-architecture/execution-stitching-and-fallback-orchestration-2026
- runbooks/runtime-upgrade-validation-and-canary-matrix-2026

Notes for reviewers:

- Please review the memory budgets table in infra/benchmarks/hardware-profiles and confirm the small/large model cutoffs align with recent capacity planning.
- Confirm that the quantized fidelity test (top-5 token agreement threshold) is still appropriate for our customer SLAs.
